title: Policy reconciliation ordering causes per-org override to suppress hard-limit enforcement during shard failover
creator: Leah Kim
description:
Summary: During a cross-shard lease handover we observed a large tenant temporarily escape its hard per-org request limit and receive significantly more tokens than allowed. This ticket tracks investigation, mitigation, and a permanent fix for a policy reconciliation ordering bug that can silently demote hard limits to grace-window (soft) behavior for affected keys.

Observed behavior: On shard failover, the new shard instance applied a recently-removed per-org override after applying a grace-window merge, causing the effective enforcement mode to be 'soft' for ~10s while the shard replayed tombstoned overrides. Customer-visible impact included token over-allowance and billing discrepancies.

Why this is different from other rate anomalies: Existing incidents often involved double-counting, duplicate debits, or cache collisions. This issue is specifically about the chronological ordering of policy tombstones and merge-pass semantics in the reconciliation path so that a removed hard-limit becomes a soft grace-window for a short window instead of being strictly enforced as removed.
investigation_steps: Reproduced in staging by forcing lease transfer between edge-shards with a per-org override add->remove sequence (steps recorded in replay-script-991357.sh)
Captured raft/lease logs from both shards around failover window (logs: gs://redwood-logs/incidents/ENG-991357/)
Added verbose policy-engine tracing to runtime build and replayed synthetic request stream to observe merge ordering (PR link below)
Compared enforcement state machine traces against expected specification in policy-spec.md (Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/RE/Policy+Merge+Spec)
Queried billing-aggregator for token attribution during the window to confirm over-allow and invoice variance
findings: Root cause: reconciliation applies tombstone (removal) and grace-window merges in separate passes. The removal pass is gated on async index compaction, while grace-window merges are applied immediately, leading to a transient state where grace-window semantics are present without the hard-limit removal having been finalized.

Edge case: if a per-org hard limit was removed and then re-added within the same shard epoch, tombstone replay ordering could end up applying the re-add after a grace-window merge, resurrecting an unintended soft-allow window.
Telemetry shows ~0.03% of failovers in the last 30d exhibited the same ordering pattern; three customers saw measurable over-allow and disputed charges.
The issue is deterministic under forced lease handoff timings but racier under real traffic; reproducer attached.
mitigation: Hotfix deployed to staging that makes tombstone removals idempotent and applies removal markers ahead of any grace-window merges (hotfix branch: github.com/redwood/re/runtime@hotfix/ENG-991357)
Emergency rollout plan prepared to flip reconciliation ordering at runtime via feature flag 'policy_reconcile_strict_order'
Short-term config: enable stricter tombstone-forwarding on edge-shards in all regions to reduce probability of window (feature flag enabled for affected tenants)
Customer outreach: billing team to issue targeted credits for affected customers; SOC and CSM notified
proposed_fix: Refactor policy reconciliation to a single ordered pass that processes mutation events in strict commit-sequence order: tombstones -> adds -> grace-window merges are applied atomically per-namespace. Add end-to-end invariant tests and a deterministic simulation harness for cross-shard replay. Implement a durable marker so that removals are visible to new shard owners before they accept traffic.
tests: integration: policy-replay-deterministic-suite (added testcases for remove->grace->readd sequences)
load: replay 10k RPS synthetic workload against two-shard failover scenario
fuzz: event-ordering fuzz harness with 100k random permutations to assert no soft-allow windows
rollout_plan: Canary: enable strict-ordered-policy-reconcile feature flag in staging and one low-traffic region (72h) with metric gating
Monitor: per-org enforcement variance, throttle-violation counts, and billing delta dashboards (Console dashboard: /dashboards/ENG-991357)
Gradual: roll flags to 25%, 50%, 100% over 7 days if no regressions
Fallback: feature flag off reverts to previous behavior; post-deploy runbook updated
postmortem_followup: Add cross-shard policy tombstone visibility metric to alerting (SLO: <1 false-positive per month)
Product: reconsider per-org override UX to include stronger invariants for add/remove within short windows
Billing: automated reconciliation job to adjust invoices for confirmed over-allow windows
Engineering: dedicate 2 sprint-weeks for simulation harness and additional invariant tests
notes: SRE recommended increasing lease transfer draining to 15s as a temporary mitigation while the fix lands
PM approved customer credits and comms plan; legal reviewed messaging for affected invoices
Design: no UI changes required for Console, but an entry explaining grace-window semantics will be added to docs
